macros.name: city
macros.doc: may be used to specify the city and country, where the author or the authors live.

macros.name: comment
macros.doc: May be used to specify some comment on the problem (e. g. the authors original comment.)

macros.name: cond
macros.doc: May be used to specify the fairy conditions of a problem.

macros.name: condition
macros.doc: May be used to specify the fairy conditions of a problem.

macros.name: DefinePieces
macros.doc: The characters used to specify color, piece and rotation may be changed using the \DefinePieces command.

macros.name: diagnum
macros.doc: This macro expects a number as a parameter. The number will be used to (re-)initialize the diagram number counter.

macros.name: dianamestyle
macros.doc: Using \dianamestyle (or \solnamestyle) you may specify how authornames are written above the boards (or before the solutions).

macros.name: genre
macros.doc: May be used to specify genre of the problem.

macros.name: gridchess
macros.doc: displays lines to seperates fieldsections for gridchess.

macros.name: gridlines
macros.doc: You may specify a list of horizontal or vertical lines within the diagram.

macros.name: horizontalcylinder
macros.doc: \horizontalcylinder suppresses the drawing of the vertical lines of the outer frame.

macros.name: issue
macros.doc: May be used to specify e. g. the issue of a magazine where the problem was issued.

macros.name: judgement
macros.doc: May be used to describe the judgement given for a problem, e. g. when you are working on an award or when you are selecting problems for a “best of . . . ” book.

macros.name: label
macros.doc: This overrides the normal \label definition such that the diagram number is displayed when using \ref instead of the page number.

macros.name: nofields
macros.doc: You may remove single fields by using the \nofields or \nosquares command.

macros.name: noframe
macros.doc: Using \noframe completely supresses the outer frame.

macros.name: noinnerframe
macros.doc: \noinnerframe suppresses the innerframe.

macros.name: nosquares
macros.doc: You may remove single fields by using the \nofields or \nosquares command.

macros.name: pages
macros.doc: May be used to specify the page (or pages) where the problem was issued.

macros.name: pieces
macros.doc: With \pieces you specify the position to be displayed on the board.

macros.name: rem
macros.doc: May be used to specify remarks to the problem.

macros.name: solnamestyle
macros.doc: Using \dianamestyle (or \solnamestyle) you may specify how authornames are written above the boards (or before the solutions).

macros.name: solution
macros.doc: \solution may be used to specify the solution of the problem.

macros.name: source
macros.doc: May be used to specify the book or magazine where the problem was issued first.

macros.name: sourceindex
macros.doc: The source register is inserted into the text using \sourceindex and the theme register using \themeindex.

macros.name: sourcenr
macros.doc: May be used to specify the number which was used for the problem inside an originals section.

macros.name: specialdiagnum
macros.doc: May be used to suppress the default diagram numbering (which uses a counter) and instead directly providing a diagram “number” which may be an arbritary text.

macros.name: stip
macros.doc: is used to specify the stipulation of the problem, e. g. \stipulation{\#2} may be used to specify a mate in two.

macros.name: stipulation
macros.doc: is used to specify the stipulation of the problem, e. g. \stipulation{\#2} may be used to specify a mate in two.

macros.name: switchcolors
macros.doc: For convenience we provide a command switchcolors which switches the value of the switchcolors boolean to true.

macros.name: themeindex
macros.doc: The source register is inserted into the text using \sourceindex and the theme register using \themeindex.

macros.name: themes
macros.doc: May be used to specify themes displayed in the problem.

macros.name: twins
macros.doc: May be used to specify the different twins of a problem.

macros.name: verticalcylinder
macros.doc: When using \verticalcylinder the horizontal lines of the outer frame will not be drawn.

envs.name: figurine
envs.doc: Instead of using the diagram, stereodiagram or spacediagram environment one may use the figurine environment. This suppresses the diagram output and produces a figurine notation inside the current text.
